key_claims.claim: Postpartum hemorrhage incidence increased from 8.1% to 10.4% and severe PPH from 0.9% to 1.3% across a large health system from 2016 to 2023, concurrent with rising induction rates and maternal comorbidities
Reducing triplets to singleton results in preeclampsia rates around 2%, compared to approximately 10% in non-reduced triplets or twins reduced from triplets

In expectantly managed preterm preeclampsia, proteinuria of 5 grams or more per 24 hours is associated with approximately 5 days shorter latency and 28% maternal complication rate versus 9% with proteinuria under 3 grams
Escalating antihypertensive treatment during expectant management of early-onset severe preeclampsia is associated with worse maternal outcomes, likely as a severity marker
Higher maternal BMI is independently associated with greater cumulative oxytocin dose and higher maximum infusion rates during labor induction in nulliparous women
